A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLOWERS research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE prediction experiments, autoregressive rollouts, model-scaling results and architectural ablations, with additional conditioned-prediction and Helmholtz results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds benchmark results, longer-rollout evaluations, data-efficiency experiments and further architectural analyses.

M1.justification: The pointwise displacement predictor, multihead pullbacks, value projections, residual blocks and multiscale architecture are unchanged. Bilinear interpolation and boundary handling receive additional documentation. Non-learned warps are introduced as an experimental control, not as a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Table 1 expands from 16 to 18 datasets by adding PDEGym CE-RM and Wave Layer, extending the existing flow-and-wave coverage. The earlier datasets, conditioned tasks, scaling benchmark and Helmholtz evaluation remain.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds a non-learned, randomly initialized warp control to the comparison with the full model. The external comparator sets remain unchanged: FNO, CNextU-Net/CNUNET and scOT in benchmarking, and POSEIDON-L in the scaling study.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation design through a 21:60 rollout window and training-data sweeps at 5%, 10%, 20%, 50% and 100% on three datasets. These are added protocols; the retained experiments keep their stated metrics, model configurations, learning-rate search and training budgets.

E4.justification: Beyond the new random-warp control, Appendix A.4.1 tests data efficiency, Table 9 extends the existing single-scale ablation from Rayleigh-Benard to three additional datasets, and Figure 13 examines multiple learned heads across three problems. These substantially broaden evidence about adaptivity, data requirements, multiscale structure and interpretability.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed accuracy estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. Throughput error bars remain standard deviations across datasets in v1 Figure 7 and v2 Figure 8; the added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 next-step and 1:20 scores are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results for longer rollouts, PDEGym, data efficiency and ablations. New long-rollout findings include FNO outperforming FLOWERS on supernova simulations at steps 21–60: 1.6350 versus 2.0709 VRMSE. The non-learned-warp control reports 0.2190 next-step and 0.4138 rollout VRMSE.

T1.justification: The characteristic expansion, kinetic-limit derivation and wave parametrix are retained. v1 Appendix C's convolution argument moves into v2 Section 3.1.1, with its finite-head sum made explicit. This restatement and the characteristic derivative-notation clarification do not substantively change the mathematics; the new mechanism discussion remains heuristic.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims: sparse adaptive warps suffice for strong PDE solvers, connect to three physical perspectives, scale to 3D and compete with larger foundation models. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 replaces largely unexplained diffusion and Helmholtz performance with proposed kinetic-collision and frequency-domain ray interpretations, explicitly qualified as heuristic. It adds structured-grid and boundary-condition limitations and revises the assessment of rollout quality. Figure 13 further qualifies interpretability as clearest in laminar, transport-dominated regimes.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, specifies bilinear sampling, and explains periodic wrapping, zero-valued out-of-domain sampling and mixed boundary handling. Table 5 supplies learning rates for the added PDEGym tasks. The new parameter-count table mainly consolidates information already stated in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused connections to multigrid/AMG, latent encoder-decoder operator learning and kinetic interpretations of attention, with corresponding references. The central positioning of adaptive pullbacks relative to Fourier, convolution and attention methods remains. Numerous other bibliography edits update publication metadata rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: The introduction and limitations are substantially rewritten, Section 3.3's kinetic explanation is condensed, and the former convolution appendix becomes main-text Section 3.1.1. New appendix subsections and consistent SELFWARP terminology further reorganize the narrative beyond simple additions of results.

P2.justification: v2 expands and reformats Table 1, adds the data-efficiency figure/table and multihead visualizations, restructures the single-scale results table and adds a parameter-count summary. Figures 1–2 are refined and several displays relocated. The redundant Helmholtz table is removed while its results remain in Table 4.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central adaptive-warp idea: the random-warp control tests whether learning the displacements matters, while data-efficiency and longer-rollout evaluations probe robustness and reveal additional exceptions to FLOWERS' advantage. Explicit boundary/grid limitations and code-access information improve transparency. These gains address important evidential gaps in v1, although the expanded physical explanations remain heuristic and accuracy uncertainty is still unreported.
